Bert Mizusawa

Republican candidate for Member, United States Senate, Virginia · Challenger

Retired U.S. Army major general and attorney

Bert Mizusawa is a retired U.S. Army major general and a West Point graduate who holds law and public policy degrees from Harvard. He served on the staff of the Senate Armed Services Committee and as a deputy undersecretary of the Army, advised Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign, and later worked as a CIA adviser. He ran in a three-way Republican primary on August 4, 2026, and is the Republican nominee against incumbent Democrat Mark Warner.

Where Mizusawa stands

Relationship with President Trump
Argues his ties to President Trump would give Virginia more influence. Says he would disagree with Trump in private before disagreeing with him in public.
War with Iran
Defended Trump's decision to attack Iran. Would not rule out sending U.S. ground troops, and did not firmly commit to requiring congressional authorization before more war funding.
Energy costs
Supports more domestic oil, natural gas and nuclear production, including small modular reactors, with renewable energy also part of the mix.
Data centers
Says data center developers should pay the full cost of the infrastructure their projects need, rather than passing those costs to other utility customers.
Housing
Proposes ending the capital gains tax on sales of primary residences. Argues this would increase housing supply and lower home prices and rents.
Healthcare and Medicaid
Proposes tying federal Medicaid funding to whether states can account for their spending. Supports telemedicine and AI to improve rural healthcare access.
Elections
Supports requiring photo ID to vote. Said he would concede if certified results, after any recounts or court challenges, showed Warner had won.
Tariffs and trade
Supports tariffs on countries he considers unfair trading partners. Opposes blanket tariffs on every nation.
